title: ExecuteSQL range without BETWEEN
description: Performance rule — ExecuteSQL range conditions written as >=/<= instead of BETWEEN make the engine evaluate two separate conditions and intersect the results; the BETWEEN construct runs the range once and is many times faster than the two single comparisons.
author: fm-lab rules

rule.rationale: The internal SQL engine treats `field >= X AND field <= Y` as two separate conditions and intersects the result sets; `BETWEEN` is recognized as a single range scan. A community measurement on ~500k records saw a factor-88 difference (728 ms vs 8 ms, averaged over 8 runs).
rule.remediation: Replace `field >= X AND field <= Y` with `field BETWEEN X AND Y` — semantically identical (both bounds inclusive, same NULL behavior), so the rewrite can never change the result.
